record.paper_title: Traces on Operator Ideals Defined over the Class of all Banach Spaces and Related Open Problems
record.original_question: Let z(N0) be a quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideal. Determine whether every trace on LAPP_z is spectral, in the sense that for each operator S the trace is determined by the eigenvalue sequence of S through the dyadic block sums described in Section 2.4.

evidence.quote: A trace τ is called spectral if τ(S) can be reconstructed from the eigenvalue sequence (λ_n(S)) for all S ∈ A(X). More precisely, we require that τ(S) = ϕ( 1/2^k Σ_{n∈D_k} λ_n(S) ), where ϕ(a) := τ(D_a) for D_a ∈ A(ℓ2).
Problem 8. Show that all traces on LAPP_z are spectral whenever z(N0) is quasi-Banach.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $\ell_\infty(\mathbb{N}_0)$ denote bounded scalar sequences indexed by $\mathbb{N}_0=\{0,1,2,\dots\}$. A linear subspace $z(\mathbb{N}_0)\subseteq\ell_\infty(\mathbb{N}_0)$ equipped with a quasi-norm $\|\cdot\|_z$ making it complete is called a quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideal if:
(i) it contains the canonical unit vectors;
(ii) it is solid: $|a_n|\le|b_n|$ for all $n$ with $b\in z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ implies $a\in z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ and $\|a\|_z\le c\|b\|_z$;
(iii) it is invariant under the dyadic averaging shift: writing $D_k=\{2^k,2^k+1,\dots,2^{k+1}-1\}$ and $T:(a_n)\mapsto\bigl(2^{-k}\sum_{n\in D_k}a_n\bigr)_{k\ge 0}$ (or its adjoint expansion), both $T$ and its right-inverse act boundedly on $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$.

For a Banach space $X$, let $L_z^{\mathrm{APP}}(X)$ consist of operators $S\in\mathcal{L}(X)$ whose approximation-number sequence $(a_n(S))_{n\ge 0}$ belongs to $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$, with $\|S\|_{L_z^{\mathrm{APP}}}:=\|(a_n(S))\|_z$. Letting $X$ vary, $L_z^{\mathrm{APP}}$ is a quasi-Banach operator ideal. A trace on $L_z^{\mathrm{APP}}$ is a linear functional $\tau$ on the component $L_z^{\mathrm{APP}}(\ell_2)$ (extended in the standard way to all components) which vanishes on commutators $[A,B]$ whenever the trace is defined.

For a diagonal operator $D_a$ on $\ell_2$ with diagonal $a\in z(\mathbb{N}_0)$, set $\varphi(a):=\tau(D_a)$. The trace $\tau$ is called spectral if for every $S\in L_z^{\mathrm{APP}}(X)$ with eigenvalue sequence $(\lambda_n(S))_{n\ge 0}$ (counted with algebraic multiplicity and ordered by decreasing modulus),
$$\tau(S)\;=\;\varphi\!\left(\Bigl(\tfrac{1}{2^k}\sum_{n\in D_k}\lambda_n(S)\Bigr)_{k\ge 0}\right).$$

Problem. Prove that whenever $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ is a quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideal, every trace on $L_z^{\mathrm{APP}}$ is spectral in the above sense.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an explicit open problem in the literature on traces on operator ideals defined over all Banach spaces. A web search reveals related work on shift-invariant functionals on Banach sequence spaces and on traces of Marcinkiewicz-type ideals, but no source establishing spectrality of all traces on $L_z^{\mathrm{APP}}$ for general quasi-Banach shift-monotone $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ was found. It thus appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Shift-invariant functionals on Banach sequence spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Reduces the theory of traces on Marcinkiewicz operator ideals to shift-invariant functionals on sequence spaces.
status_evidence.claim: Related framework exists but does not resolve spectrality on $L_z^{APP}$ for arbitrary quasi-Banach shift-monotone $z$.

status_evidence.title: The Spectrum of Shift Operators and the Existence of Traces
status_evidence.snippet: Studies existence of traces via spectra of shift operators on sequence ideals.
status_evidence.claim: Addresses existence rather than spectrality of all traces on approximation-number ideals.

status_evidence.title: Quasi-Banach operator ideals with a very strange trace
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs continuous traces on quasi-Banach ideals with unusual properties.
status_evidence.claim: Indicates subtleties in the quasi-Banach setting relevant to whether all traces must be spectral.
